newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian grain trade doubts Cargill China wheat sale.
newsitem.headline: Asian grain trade doubts Cargill China wheat sale.

text.p: Grain dealers in Asia on Tuesday could not confirm recent rumours of sales of up to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat to China, possibly partly destined for North Korea, by U.S. trader Cargill.
"Nobody can substantiate this, it's highly unlikely and knowning the Chinese, it just doesn't add up," said one wheat trader, echoing the views of others in Hong Kong and in China.

Rumours that Cargill Inc sold between 1.0-1.5 million tonnes of optional origin wheat to China or North Korea snaked through U.S. grains markets on Friday. U.S. traders said the market shrugged off the talk.
Cargill, which has permission from the U.S. government to sell North Korea up to 500,000 tonnes of wheat or rice, has declined to comment on the market talk.
"What's the point of China buying any wheat when there is enough wheat available in the country?" said one Chinese source.

China said on Monday it expected a record summer grain harvest, and that the summer crop would represent 22 percent of the total grain harvest for the year. China has said its total grain harvest last year was 490 million tonnes.
Grains traders said that China was unlikely to spend the huge sums required to purchase 1.5 million tonnes of wheat.
"I think maybe smaller amounts have possibly been done, of Canadian wheat," said one China-based grains trader.
One veteran trader noted that although China was predisposed to helping North Korea, which is currently suffering from chronic food shortages, China's generosity was limited.
Some suggested the rumour was started to favour a long position in the market.
"It is possible," said one Beijing-based industry source.
He pointed to improving political ties between the U.S. and China and said that although there was plenty of wheat in China, the country's processing capacity was not enough.
